question.knowledge_point: Simplifying Expressions by Factoring an Alternate Form of the Pythagorean Identity
question.worked_solution:
First, we rewrite the denominator using $1-{sin}^{2}⁡x={cos}^{2}⁡x.$

$$
\frac{1-\operatorname{sin}⁡x}{{cos}^{2}⁡x}=\frac{1-\operatorname{sin}⁡x}{1-{sin}^{2}⁡x}
$$

Next, we factor the denominator as difference of squares, and simplify:

$$
\begin{aligned}\frac{1-\operatorname{sin}⁡x}{1-{sin}^{2}⁡x} & =\frac{1-\operatorname{sin}⁡x}{(1-\operatorname{sin}⁡x)(1+\operatorname{sin}⁡x)} \\  & =\frac{\cancel{1-\operatorname{sin}⁡x}}{\cancel{(1-\operatorname{sin}⁡x)}(1+\operatorname{sin}⁡x)} \\  & =\frac{1}{1+\operatorname{sin}⁡x}\end{aligned}
$$

Therefore, $f(x)=1+\operatorname{sin}⁡x.$
